### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **100** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via handleCatalogActivationWrite (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleAutomationRequest (symbol, a top-level function), handleI18nRequest (symbol, a top-level function), handleMcpRequest (symbol, a top-level function), handleMetadataRequest (symbol, a top-level function), handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function), handlePermissionSetCloneWrite (symbol, a top-level function), handleSecurityRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json adb65d1615dc0698d7b52a113831221bbc187d9f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `02bb318bb50053d3109ab0e3e83afd5d59116e89` — the merge of head `b30bbb0ffba65788668c9bbe4fc42dc086504628` into base `adb65d1615dc0698d7b52a113831221bbc187d9f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 02bb318bb50053d3109ab0e3e83afd5d59116e89 && git checkout 02bb318bb50053d3109ab0e3e83afd5d59116e89
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin adb65d1615dc0698d7b52a113831221bbc187d9f b30bbb0ffba65788668c9bbe4fc42dc086504628 && git checkout -B drift-repro adb65d1615dc0698d7b52a113831221bbc187d9f && git merge --no-ff b30bbb0ffba65788668c9bbe4fc42dc086504628

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json adb65d1615dc0698d7b52a113831221bbc187d9f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs adb65d1615dc0698d7b52a113831221bbc187d9f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5e4ea090492b296c22d65d0bb30fbab94ee66e73`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, auth.ts, automation.ts, catalog-activation.ts, i18n.ts, mcp.ts, meta.ts, packages.ts, permission-set-clone.ts, security.ts, share-links.ts, own-door-bridge.ts (all under packages/runtime/src/domains/), packages/runtime/src/domains/domain-501-language-37811.test.ts (the source walk only), scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs

Read: card #37811 with its three comments, the PR body, the 27-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head (all completed; none failed). The other test files, the spec test and the changeset body are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec/system`: widened.** `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` gains 37 keys in each of `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES` (31 sentences, 6 `catalog_activation_noun_*` nouns). Nothing is removed or renamed and no existing sentence changes. The export's type (`Record` of `Record`) does not move. Additive: right as a change, but see ② for how it is declared.
- **Accept set: unchanged.** No schema, no authorable key, no request shape. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- **Wire, `@objectstack/runtime`: 31 `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` answers.** Status and `error.code` are unchanged. With no `Accept-Language`, or a language the catalog holds no locale of, the `message` is the sentence the door answered before. I compared each English key with the removed literal, concatenations and the `NOUN[type].toLowerCase()` nouns included: all 31 match byte for byte. The answers gain `Vary: Accept-Language`. Right.
- **Permission-set clone landing.** The `501` thrown by `resolveDefaultCloneLanding` now carries `messageKey` and `params`, and the door answers it from an inner catch through `catalogNotImplemented`, where it went to `deps.errorFromThrown(err, 500)`. The function has no other caller in the tree, and for a throw that carries only a message and `statusCode: 501` both paths build the same envelope. Every other throw is rethrown to the outer catch unchanged. Right.
- **No consumer keys on these sentences.** No non-test code under `packages/` or `ui/` matches their English text, so a localized `message` breaks no reader.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/runtime` patch match what the diff publishes: a fix, with `Metadata-protocol: none`, and a widening that is not a protocol change ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

Clause-②: the PR body and the changeset both say `no`. That is wrong for this diff; see S1.

**S1 (should-fix) — the `Clause-②:` line says `no` on a diff that widens a published surface.** The diff adds 37 keys to `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES`, a published export. The three earlier changesets on `main` that added keys to this same catalog for this same family of doors declare `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: `.changeset/37352-own-door-501-locale.md`, `.changeset/37610-own-door-501-locale-rest.md` and `.changeset/37662-approvals-act-inbound-hooks-501-locale.md`. The one that declares `no`, `.changeset/37737-own-door-501-ja-vary.md`, added no key. The level stays `patch` either way, so nothing about the bump changes. What changes is where the release body files the entry: `scripts/release-github-releases.mjs` puts a non-breaking `yes` widening under 新增能力 and a `no` under 其他修复 (`docs/releases-maintenance.md`). Fix: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the PR body and in `.changeset/37811-domain-501-languages.md`.

### ③ Boundary flags

The card lists no `open_questions`. The dev's four flags, from the PR body's "Small calls made here":

- **`capabilityUnavailable` stays English** (ten call sites): accepted. `unavailable.ts` states the contract in its own docblock: the `501` body and discovery's `services.<slot>.message` are one sentence so they cannot drift, and discovery is English. Localizing one side alone would break that. The card asks for a stated reason for any sentence left in English, and this one is stated in the PR body and the changeset. Escalated to the seat as a follow-up, not a condition of this PR: the seat note on the card (7210862044) named these ten sites for this card, and they remain the largest English `501` family, so localizing discovery together with this answer needs its own card.
- **The MCP resume door's `501` stays English** (`mcp.ts`, `resumeDoorError`): accepted. It is thrown into the tool error mapping, and every other refusal of that door is English.
- **`meta.ts`'s `errorFromThrown(e, 501)` is not localized**: accepted. It forwards the metadata service's own thrown message; `501` is only the fallback status.
- **The activation noun has its own keys, and the verb is two keys**: accepted. The six key suffixes are exactly the six `CatalogActivationType` members, and the English nouns equal `NOUN[type].toLowerCase()`.

The card's other expectations: every one of the 31 sentence keys is asserted by a door test in the diff; Japanese says `自動化` in the five sentences that name the automation service, and `オートメーション` nowhere; review N2 of PR #37813 is done (the `requestLocaleOf` jsdoc and the four gate comments; those four modules do answer through `catalogNotImplemented` on this head, and their only direct `deps.error` calls are the sanitised 500s).

SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

Security: no private finding.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts`.** The new jsdoc paragraph holds sentence by sentence against the code.
- "read … by the request's top `Accept-Language` tag, with no `errors.*` override consulted": every site goes through `catalogNotImplemented`, which calls `operationUserMessage` with `requestLocaleOf(context)` and no `translate`.
- "Their English is byte-identical to the fixed sentences they replace": holds, as ① says.
- "`{{member}}`, `{{table}}`, `{{name}}` and `{{packageId}}` … never translated": the call sites pass a member name, `METADATA_ACTIVATION_TABLE`, the item name and the package id. `interpolateValidationMessage` fills placeholders in one pass through a replacer function, so a name that itself contains `{{…}}` or `$&` is printed as written.
- "`{{noun}}` is one of the `catalog_activation_noun_*` keys, rendered in the same locale": `catalog-activation.ts` renders the noun with the same `requestLocaleOf(context)` it hands the sentence.
- Every locale carries all 37 keys with the English placeholders, in the same order.

**The domain modules.** Each replaced site keeps its condition, its position in the door's order of checks and its status; only the builder changes. The three `501`s left on other builders are the ones ③ accepts. I looked for a way to make a door answer differently than before in English and found none.

**`own-door-bridge.ts`, `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`.** Comments only; no gate count moves. They agree with the code, except N1.

No must-fix. One should-fix, S1 above. Nits, none of which changes an answer:

- N1 (nit) — the `requestLocaleOf` jsdoc now says the non-bridge doors reach it through `catalogNotImplemented`. `catalog-activation.ts` also calls it directly, for the noun.
- N2 (nit) — the card asks for a pin per door. `handleMcpSkillRequest`'s `501` (`mcp.ts`, the skill door) has none: only `/mcp` is driven. Likewise only `catalog_activation_noun_position` is rendered through the door; the other five nouns are pinned for translation only, and nothing ties `CatalogActivationType` to the noun keys, so a seventh type would answer the raw key until its noun is added.
- N3 (nit) — `zh-CN` says `定制软件包` for the customization package in three sentences. The console's `zh-Hans` bundle says `定制包`. The card asks for the platform's existing terms.
- N4 (nit) — the source walk in `domain-501-language-37811.test.ts` counts parentheses without reading string literals, and sees only a literal `deps.error(…, 501)`. A `501` passed through a wrapper, as `resumeDoorError(deps, …, 501)` is, or through `deps.errorFromThrown(e, 501)`, is not caught. Its comment says so for the two existing cases.
- N5 (nit) — the changeset says two `501`s stay English; the PR body names three sites that are not localized (`meta.ts`'s forwarded one is the third).

N1 to N5 are left as accepted deviations or a follow-up card: a fix to any of them moves this head. S1's fix moves the head too and takes a delta review.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

What moved: one commit, `b30bbb0ffb`, on top of the reviewed head. It changes one file, `.changeset/37811-domain-501-languages.md`, by 3 lines added and 2 removed. No file on the `Scope:` line moved, so sections ①, ③ and ④ of the earlier record stand for this head as written.

### ① Derived judgments

Unchanged: the published catalog gains 37 keys, the accept set does not move, and 31 `501` answers follow the request's language with their English, status and code as before.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/runtime` patch, unchanged and right. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

Clause-②: the PR body and the changeset now both say `yes (widening)`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. That matches the diff and the three earlier changesets on this catalog.

S1: closed

The changeset also gains the `Skills-docs: none` line the PR body carries, as `37352-own-door-501-locale.md` has it.

### ③ Boundary flags

Unchanged. The follow-up escalated in the earlier record, localizing `capabilityUnavailable` together with discovery, is now card #37864.

SQL push-down: nothing to check; the delta touches no code.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N5: closed. The changeset now names the three `501`s that stay English, as the PR body does: `capabilityUnavailable`, the MCP resume door's, and the `/meta` save fallback that forwards the metadata service's thrown message.

N1, N2, N3 and N4 stand as written in the earlier record, each a nit with no effect on an answer. They are accepted deviations on this PR and are carried by card #37864.

Check-runs on this head: 59 success, 13 skipped, none failed. One `PR-body guards` run was cancelled when the body edit started its rerun, and the rerun succeeded.
